name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,137

clue.text: Sinister reason to attend an auction?

blocks.note: first meaning: threatening, unfriendly in appearance
second meaning, read as two words: you go to a sale for the purpose of making offers

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: the second sense breaks the word into FOR BIDDING, the reason people turn up at a saleroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidding looks grim and menacing, which is close to the ordinary sense of sinister.

clue.text: Additional fuss when leader is ousted

indicators.note: a leader ousted is the front-runner thrown out, so the opening letter goes

explanation.surface: Political drama: more commotion erupts as the party head is toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like news of a coup; the ousted leader is only the first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean further or extra, as in 'two other people', matching additional.

clue.text: Lower attendance ultimately seen in the NBA, strangely

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used
done strangely means done in an odd, unexpected order, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A report that basketball crowds have fallen off in the National Basketball Association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower attendance' reads as one phrase about crowd numbers, but 'Lower' alone is the definition. The NBA is the North American professional basketball league.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath and lower both mean situated under something, as prepositions or adverbs of position.

clue.text: Finally relapsed after years not drinking

indicators.note: finally points to the end of each word, so the closing letters are kept

explanation.surface: A sad recovery story: someone fell off the wagon after years of sobriety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to belong to the relapse story but governs all three following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry person or place abstains from alcohol, as in a dry January or a dry county.

clue.text: Opening new urinal around first half of month

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters take a fresh form
around means encircling, so one group of letters wraps another
only the front half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A ribbon-cutting for a brand-new public toilet sometime in the early part of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like a noun for the ceremony but is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event is the first one, marking a beginning, so it is an opening speech or match.

clue.text: Elaborate stage entrances

indicators.note: to elaborate is to work something up into a new, developed form

explanation.surface: A theatre direction calling for showy, grand arrivals of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrances' looks like an actor's arrival on stage; it is the plural noun for ways in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gates are openings in a fence or wall through which people enter, hence entrances.

clue.text: Spoil one politician with caviar every so often

indicators.note: every so often means at intervals, so alternate letters are picked

explanation.surface: A lobbyist corrupting a legislator with occasional gifts of caviar.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is a Member of Parliament, in Canada as in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or weaken it, which is what spoiling does.

clue.text: Lightweight, extremely glossy doodah

indicators.note: extremely read as at the extremes, so only the outermost letters count

explanation.surface: A description of a flimsy, very shiny gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely glossy' reads as very shiny, but extremely means the extremes of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual placeholder words for an object whose proper name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Fall for a New Yorker?

blocks.note: surface reading: a tumble, or falling in love with someone from New York, or the magazine
setter's reading: the season an American calls fall, translated into the other English name

explanation.walkthrough: Americans call the season between summer and winter 'fall'; the clue asks for the word the rest of the English-speaking world uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The season Americans name fall is known elsewhere by its other name, so the clue is a translation.

clue.text: Sea creature netted in major catch

indicators.note: something netted is caught inside, so the letters sit enclosed in the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A fisherman's boast about hauling in a big sea animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishing surface fits the definition, so the solver hunts for a fish rather than reading the letters in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a large marine mammal, so it is a creature of the sea.

clue.text: A-list celeb from Ramsgate, unusually

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon manner, so the letters are set out in an uncommon order

blocks.note: Ramsgate is a seaside town in Kent, England

explanation.surface: A surprising piece of gossip: a top celebrity hails from a small English seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramsgate, a modest resort town in Kent, is an unlikely home for a superstar, which is the joke of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is a hugely famous performer, the kind of person at the top of any guest list.

clue.text: Crooked con man is stealing millions to get large, modern house

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into another order
to steal is to take something in and hold it, so one piece goes inside

explanation.surface: A swindler embezzles a fortune and buys himself a big new house.
explanation.walkthrough: The crooked con man reads as a single figure, but 'Crooked' signals the shuffle of 'con man is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A McMansion is a derisive North American term for a big, mass-produced suburban home lacking character.

clue.text: Get to the bottom of six feet of water?

blocks.note: first meaning: understand fully, work out
second meaning: a unit of depth at sea equal to six feet

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense of understanding comes from the same idea as sounding the seabed, which makes the two halves blur into one nautical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand a mystery is to get to its bottom; the nautical depth unit measures six feet.

clue.text: Second-rate aircon in Australia is something you can count on

indicators.note: being in something means being enclosed by it

explanation.surface: A complaint that inferior air conditioning in Australia is at least reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something you can count on' sounds like a dependable thing; it is literally a device for counting.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for doing arithmetic, so you literally do sums on it.

clue.text: Casual comment about work on exam papers?

explanation.surface: An offhand observation on the chore of grading tests.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the answer also reads as RE-MARK, grading the scripts again.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a brief spoken observation, the kind of passing comment made in conversation.

clue.text: Drink from market in India

blocks.note: a mart is a trading place
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Buying a beverage at a bazaar in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a position word but is taken literally as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth, so it is an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: For example, one red-coloured finch

blocks.note: first meaning: a counting number such as one, two or three
second meaning: a bright red North American songbird

explanation.walkthrough: 'For example, one' seems to introduce the bird; it is a definition by example of a counting number. The bird's name also comes from the red robes of Catholic prelates.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers like one are called cardinal numbers; the red crested songbird of North America shares the name.

clue.text: Launch of university beset by financial liability

indicators.note: beset means surrounded on all sides, so one piece is hemmed in by another

explanation.surface: A new college starting up already saddled with money troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch of university' reads as one phrase; 'Launch' alone is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance or introduction, which is what launching something amounts to.

clue.text: Went by bike, or maybe went by dinghy, by the sounds of it?

indicators.note: what something sounds like is how it is heard spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: a small boat is propelled with oars

explanation.surface: Two ways a person might have travelled: on two wheels or in a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves look like definitions; only the cycling one is, and the boating one sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode is the past tense of ride, used for travelling on a bicycle as well as a horse.

clue.text: Compact earth at the base of animal hideouts

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: Packed soil found at the bottom of burrows.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'at the base of' puts the earth letter below the lairs. 'Compact' looks like a verb but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something compact is closely packed together, which is what dense describes.

clue.text: Family member heads for Bologna, an Italian city

indicators.note: heads are the tops or fronts, so the opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: A relative sets off on a trip to an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An Italian city' points at Italy, but 'an' and 'Italian' are only first letters; the city is in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbai, formerly Bombay, is the largest city of India and its commercial capital.

clue.text: Day with close pal

explanation.surface: Spending a day with a best mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close pal' reads as one phrase meaning best friend; 'close' is the noun meaning conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is an informal word for a companion or mate, the same thing as a friend.

clue.text: Price offered regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is picked

explanation.surface: A shop's standing price, the one quoted every time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price offered' looks like one phrase; 'offered' is only the source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a charge paid for a service, which is a kind of price.

clue.text: Fork prongs picking up passion fruit

indicators.note: to pick something up is to take hold of it, so one piece holds another

explanation.surface: Spearing pieces of passion fruit with a fork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passion fruit' wants to be read as one thing; 'passion' is the inserted piece and 'fruit' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerines are small, easily peeled citrus fruits related to the mandarin orange.
